why: Canary 1.1 introduces a sustained 5xx regression on the checkout path. Evidence from the 120s / 9814-request load test: canary served 10 5xx (0.41% overall) while stable served 0 across 7359 requests. All 10 errors are on /checkout: canary 10/483 = 2.07% vs stable 0/1455 = 0.00% on the same endpoint; /browse and /search were clean on both versions, so the failure is endpoint-specific rather than noise spread across traffic. The per-window breakdown shows canary 5xx in every window (1, 3, 3, 3 for 0-30s, 30-60s, 60-90s, 90-120s) while stable stayed at 0 in all windows, so this is persistent and not a cold-start or warmup blip that would fade. Latency is not the issue and does not offset this: canary vs stable p50/p95/p99 are effectively identical overall (28/96/105 vs 32/94/104) and per route (/browse 22/27/28 vs 21/27/28, /search 46/58/60 both, /checkout 83/104/106 vs 82/104/106), and canary p95 tracks stable within ~1-5ms in every window. Judgement: zero errors on 1455 stable checkout requests versus 10 on 483 canary requests is far outside what sampling noise would produce, and checkout is the revenue-critical path where a 2% failure rate means real customers cannot complete purchases. Promoting to 100% would multiply that failure onto all checkout traffic, so the cost of a bad promote clearly exceeds the cost of delaying the release. Recommend rolling back the 1.1 pod, reproducing the checkout 5xx from the canary pod logs/traces, and re-running the canary after a fix.
